data.name: Alhama
data.gender_notes: Alhama is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root words 'al' which means 'the' and 'hama' which means 'exalted'. The name Alhama is often given to a child born near water or to a child who is expected to bring peace and calmness to the family. The name Alhama carries the meaning “The Exalted One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Alhama usually hope their child will grow to embody the exalted one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Signifying spiritual elevation and inner peace.
data.etymology: Alhama belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Exalted One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alhama total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

In modern times, it remains a popular choice among Muslim parents seeking a name that embodies spiritual significance and positive attributes.
